name: Green municipalism
summary: Green municipalism holds that ecological change should be built from the city or town up, through grassroots municipal institutions, rather than waiting for national or state policy. It joins green values (ecological limits, participatory democracy, nonviolence, social justice) with municipal self-government, public or community control of local essentials and direct citizen participation.
scope: The green strand of municipalism: Brian Milani's Designing the Green Economy (2000) and the 1992 Syracuse/Onondaga Green Party platform, as practised by green and left municipalist city parties (Barcelona en Comu, Projet Montreal and similar). Green-party positions are taken from the Global Greens Charter, and the assembly and confederal model from Bookchin's libertarian municipalism. Many answers outside local democracy and ecology are inferred from the Green program, so confidence is lower there.

sources.title: Green municipalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition (environmental change arising from municipal rather than state or national action), origins in Milani's 2000 book and the 1992 Syracuse Greens platform, and the municipalist parties that follow it.

sources.title: Libertarian Municipalism: An Overview
sources.author: Murray Bookchin
sources.usedFor: Assemblies, recallable confederal deputies, community custody of land and enterprise, rejection of nationalization and of the state, and the ecological critique of capitalism.

sources.title: Global Greens Charter: Political Action
sources.author: Global Greens, via Asia Pacific Greens Federation
sources.usedFor: The green-party program on the economy, trade, corporations, war and nuclear power, gender, minorities, Indigenous peoples, animals, rights and local government.

sources.title: Libertarian municipalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Summary of the parent theory: municipalization, confederalism, rejection of nationalization, and property as a source of exploitation.

sources.title: Global Greens Charter
sources.author: Global Greens
sources.usedFor: The core values: ecological wisdom, social justice, equality, freedom, participatory democracy, nonviolence, sustainability and respect for diversity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a municipal-level doctrine; Green program keeps essentials public and rejects treating health as a tradable commodity, which points toward guaranteed care, though delivery would be local.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Global Greens back workers' rights and social justice, so higher wage floors fit, but the sources give no wage-level position.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Bookchin says capitalism's grow-or-die market imperative is incompatible with ecological limits, so adherents reject the claim that markets allocate better than collective decision.

public-ownership.rationale: Bookchin rejects nationalized enterprise as centralization and wants community custody instead, though Green programs keep water and essentials publicly owned, so state-level public ownership is disfavoured but not condemned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Green program calls for a financial transactions tax and an end to policies that favour the rich, which implies heavier taxation of wealth and speculation.

unions-good.rationale: The Global Greens political action section supports workers' right to unionise.

property-fundamental.rationale: Municipalism treats private property as a source of exploitation and places land and enterprise in community custody, so an inviolable property right is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Global Greens say corporations have outsized influence over governments and want them bound to the strictest environmental, labour and social laws and tried in an international court for ecological destruction.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social justice is a core Green principle and the program supports community economies and protection of the vulnerable, so cutting welfare is opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Bookchin explicitly rejects syndicalist worker-controlled firms in favour of community custody, while Green community-economy advocates favour cooperatives, so adherents differ.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Greens stress civil liberties and accountability for abuses; the sources do not discuss surveillance, so this is inferred from those principles.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The Green program page does not address drug policy and green parties vary, so there is no firm position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Greens favour respect for diversity and minority rights but also civil liberties; the sources do not address speech law, and adherents are divided.

strong-leader.rationale: Bookchin's model puts power in face-to-face assemblies and recallable deputies, and Greens commit to participatory democracy, so a leader bypassing deliberation is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Bookchin calls the state an alien coercive formation to be displaced by confederated municipalities, but green municipalists in practice govern city councils, so the strand is only partly anti-state.

limit-guns.rationale: Greens favour nonviolence and arms-trade regulation; gun ownership itself is not discussed, so this is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Global Greens commit to nonviolence, aim to eliminate the arms trade and want military force used only as a last resort, so more police-military funding is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Global Greens oppose the sale of sex as an economic-security strategy but green parties differ on legalisation; the sources do not settle it.

decide-locally.rationale: Green municipalism's defining claim is that change should arise from the municipality rather than state or national policy; Bookchin and the Greens both back strengthening local government.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Green program opposes the death penalty and supports accountability for torturers; prison purpose is not discussed, so rehabilitation is inferred from its humane rights stance.

traditional-family.rationale: Greens stress respect for diversity and marriage equality, implying no privileged family form, though the sources do not discuss family structure directly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Global Greens political action section supports marriage equality and decriminalising same-sex relations.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Global Greens back women's right to control their fertility.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of state and religion, so a larger public role for religion is disfavoured.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Global Greens commit to defending the rights of people of colour and to compensation for displaced Indigenous peoples, supporting active redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Greens support legal recognition of transgender people and gender mainstreaming, but the sources do not state a view on gender's origin.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Greens emphasise local communities and respect for diversity over national culture, but preservation of local culture is valued; the national frame is not their focus.

gradual-change.rationale: Bookchin calls for a dual power challenging state legitimacy and a radical break from statecraft, though municipal electoral work is incremental; adherents differ on pace.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Global Greens call for protection for asylum seekers and a ban on collective expulsion, so cuts in immigration are opposed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Global Greens want the UN strengthened and the ICC supported, though they want multilateral bodies democratised.

free-trade.rationale: The Global Greens oppose new WTO-rules trade deals and want environmental, labour and health agreements to override trade rules.

nation-first.rationale: Greens want strengthened global partnership and UN institutions and base politics on local communities rather than nation-state interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The Greens allow force only as a last resort against genocide or mass abuse under a UN mandate, a narrow yes that sits against their nonviolence; adherents are divided.

open-borders.rationale: Greens defend asylum seekers and oppose collective expulsion, but the sources do not call for open borders; municipalists differ.

limit-growth.rationale: The Global Greens recognise ecological limits to material growth, call for well-being rather than GDP as the measure of progress, and Bookchin condemns capitalism's grow-or-die imperative.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The Global Greens make ecological wisdom and sustainability core principles and call for a circular zero-waste economy and eco-taxes; green municipalism makes environmental action its purpose.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Greens stress ecological limits and redesign of the economy rather than technological fixes, so faith that technology will solve most problems is rejected.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The Global Greens political action text opposes any expansion of nuclear power and calls for its phase-out.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bookchin speaks of dual power and a subterranean civil war between state and community but works through municipal elections and assemblies; the Greens commit to nonviolence.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bookchin wants citizens, not experts or representatives, to decide in face-to-face assemblies, and Greens commit to participatory democracy.

central-planning.rationale: Bookchin rejects nationalized, centralized economies as a collectivised form of the privatized economy and wants decisions made in municipal assemblies.

socialized-markets.rationale: Bookchin wants community custody and no market logic, while Green community-economy advocates accept cooperative markets; the strand is divided.

land-value-tax.rationale: Green parties sometimes support land taxes among eco-taxes, but the sources do not mention a land value tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Green social-justice aims and anti-concentration of wealth; the sources do not discuss inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Many green parties back basic income but the sources do not mention it and municipalists favour local provision.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Greens oppose WTO liberalisation and favour local economies, but ecological aims also oppose protecting polluting industry; adherents differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Bookchin rejects centralised state direction of the economy, though Green programs favour public green investment; municipal rather than national direction is preferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Municipalists want land and enterprise in community custody rather than small private owners or corporations, so neither side of the claim fits cleanly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bookchin invokes from each according to ability but leaves distribution to be settled in practice; Greens favour community economies, not abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Green program favours public control of finance and a transactions tax, opposing leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class bodies setting wages conflict with assembly-based decision-making, but the sources do not discuss corporatism directly.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Global Greens commit to participatory democracy and respect for diversity, which excludes a single guiding party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rule by hereditary office contradicts Bookchin's assembly democracy and the Green participatory-democracy principle.

democracy-best.rationale: Greens commit to participatory democracy, but municipalists criticise representative democracy and the claim that voters may choose badly is not addressed.

direct-votes.rationale: Bookchin wants citizens deciding policy directly in face-to-face assemblies rather than through representatives.

workers-councils.rationale: Bookchin rejects syndicalist workers' control and wants citizen assemblies of the whole community, not workers' bodies, as the base of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Municipal confederation lets a majority block local actions violating rights, and Greens favour local autonomy, but secession itself is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bookchin's turn from passive constituents to active citizens in assemblies implies that every citizen is fit to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nonviolence is a Global Greens core principle, but Bookchin speaks of dual power and a civil war between state and society, so adherents differ on absolute renunciation.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nonviolence is a core Global Greens principle, so war as character-building is rejected.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of state and religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Greens support separation of religion and state and respect for diversity, ruling out scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Green municipalism wants public matters handled by citizens' assemblies, not private firms, and Greens want corporate power curbed.

military-superiority.rationale: The Global Greens want arms reduced, arms trade eliminated and space demilitarised.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Respect for diversity is a core Green principle and municipalism builds politics on shared citizenship rather than ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bookchin argues class divisions should give way to a general interest in citizenship and ecology, rejecting class struggle as the central driver; Green sources give no statement.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Greens stress social justice and equality, but the sources do not specify outcomes versus opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The Global Greens support Indigenous self-determination, land rights and the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples as a minimum standard.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Greens back compensation for displaced peoples and debt-relief reform, but state reparations for colonialism are not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Greens favour global partnership and local communities over civilizational blocs; inferred from that stance.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Bookchin wants citizens to think in terms of community rather than personal interests, and Greens reject consumerism and profit-first economics.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Global Greens push to expand individual rights, including a right to a healthy environment, though community responsibility is stressed.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecological wisdom is a core Global Greens principle, and Green politics values nature in itself, not only as a resource.

limit-population.rationale: The Global Greens' population discussion proposes rural development and no population-control measures, and adherents differ.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Bookchin condemns capitalism's grow-or-die logic but celebrates technology's liberatory potential; Greens call for transformation, not rejection of industrial society.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Green program stresses ecological limits and caution, so speeding up disruptive technological change is opposed.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources do not address human enhancement and Green opinion varies.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Bookchin's face-to-face assembly democracy places decisions with citizens, not algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from Green civil-liberties commitments; the sources do not mention encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Greens aim to build a new sustainable society and pursue social justice and equality, so restoration of a lost order is rejected.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Green municipalism frames itself as a philosophy of local action, but pragmatic municipal governance is common; the sources do not state a view.

direct-action.rationale: Bookchin favours municipal electoral politics and assemblies over parliamentary parties at the national level, and Greens use elections; direct action is not their defining method.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bookchin's libertarian municipalism builds assemblies now as the seed of the future society, a prefigurative approach, and the Greens link nonviolent means to their ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Greens seek a sustainable circular economy and well-being, not a return to hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Bookchin speaks of overcoming vocational interests in citizenship but does not call for abolishing the division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Bookchin cites from each according to ability and leaves distribution to be settled in practice; this points toward need-based sharing but is not a firm commitment.

production-for-use.rationale: Bookchin's critique of the market's grow-or-die imperative and community custody of enterprise imply production for social and ecological needs, not profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Bookchin treats class divisions as less central than citizenship and ecology, and Green sources make no claim about profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bookchin rejects statecraft and class-based dictatorship in favour of assemblies of all citizens.

collective-farming.rationale: Bookchin wants land in community custody but the sources do not say how it is farmed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Bookchin condemns capitalism's grow-or-die imperative but the sources do not discuss imperialist war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Greens support eco-taxes, a financial transactions tax and public provision, so taxation is not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Greens accept restrictions for ecological and social ends beyond direct harm to others, but also stress civil liberties; adherents differ.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Global Greens endorse the collective rights of Indigenous peoples and linguistic minorities as well as individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Greens commit to nonviolence and limited military force, so state conscription is disfavoured.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Bookchin and the Greens put democratic voice in assemblies and participation at the centre, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Green programs keep essentials public, reject commodification of health and education and oppose corporate influence.

positive-liberty.rationale: Greens stress social justice and the material conditions of participation, though the sources do not state the freedom concept.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Global Greens say corporations hold outsized influence over governments; the claim about universities and media is not addressed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Global Greens defend people of colour and respect for diversity, so genetic racial hierarchies are rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Bookchin wants recallable deputies from citizen assemblies, not family or trade bodies, though local community representation appeals.

total-state.rationale: Bookchin rejects the state as an alien coercive apparatus and wants decisions at the local level.

national-rebirth.rationale: Greens look to an ecological, participatory future built from local communities, not nationalist rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Global Greens want arms reduced and force used only as a last resort.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by oaths of loyalty contradicts assembly democracy and citizen equality.

bound-labor.rationale: Social justice and equality are core Global Greens values, and the program supports workers' rights.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The sources do not address epistemology and Greens differ.

universal-morality.rationale: Respect for diversity and ecological ethics are stressed, but the sources do not address moral universals.

single-common-good.rationale: Bookchin sees ecology as a common interest cutting across class, gender and ethnic lines, yet the Greens' respect for diversity means plural interests; adherents differ.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources do not address Israel; the Greens' stance on self-determination and rights is general.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources do not address diaspora return, though Greens favour refugee protection.

revive-national-language.rationale: Greens support minority language rights, but state revival of national languages is not addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Bookchin wants public decisions on economic life taken by citizens and Green programs favour democratic community economies, though not through workers alone.

school-vouchers.rationale: Greens reject treating education as a tradable commodity, which tells against vouchers, though the sources do not discuss them.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Greens criticise neo-liberal austerity thinking and favour public investment, but the sources do not discuss deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Greens criticise financialised neo-liberal capitalism, so they reject the claim that political freedom depends on economic freedom in the market sense.

rule-by-example.rationale: Bookchin wants institutional democratic structures with confederal rules, not reliance on rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: Greens support self-determination for Indigenous peoples but prefer local and global levels to the nation-state; the sources do not settle national statehood.

force-without-un.rationale: The Global Greens allow force only under a UN mandate.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources do not address faith versus reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Global Greens call for protection for asylum seekers and rights for all, so reserving welfare to citizens is rejected.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from social-justice commitments; the sources do not discuss workfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bookchin wants class divisions to give way to citizenship, but also opposes capitalists' power; the sources do not state this directly.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Respect for diversity and ecological wisdom favour preserving cultural inheritance, not sacrificing it.

dominated-front.rationale: Greens favour global partnership and multilateral reform and the sources do not address civilizational fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Greens favour international solidarity and global governance reform.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights, political participation and gender mainstreaming.

ban-interest.rationale: Greens critique finance and speculation but the sources do not call for banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Global Greens commit to defending the rights of people of colour and respect for diversity, which excludes legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Bookchin calls the state a coercive apparatus above the people but frames the conflict as state versus community rather than class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Global Greens call for a circular zero-waste economy, eco-taxes and ecological limits, and green municipalism has environmental action as its purpose.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Respect for diversity and linguistic minority rights are Global Greens commitments, contradicting forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Global Greens support asylum and diversity and nothing in the sources supports replacement conspiracies.

proportional-representation.rationale: Green parties widely favour proportional representation, but the sources do not state it and municipalists focus on assemblies.

national-mission.rationale: The Global Greens favour global partnership and multilateralism rather than national missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and treat sexualised violence as a war crime, in line with structural gender inequality.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Municipalists criticise career politicians and representative parties and want citizens to govern directly, though the sources do not claim corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Respect for diversity and disability rights make eugenic limits unacceptable.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Global Greens call for accountability for torturers and for war crimes such as sexualised violence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Greens want public control of essentials, social justice policy and strengthened local government, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Global Greens defend people of colour and respect for diversity, which excludes discouraging mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality and social justice are core Global Greens values.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed by municipalist or Green sources.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Global Greens back Indigenous self-determination and land rights but no source applies the colonial label to settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Greens support religious pluralism and secular state, but the sources do not discuss civil codes.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Greens support separation of state and religion and respect for diversity, so restricting conversion is rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Greens call for humane treatment in slaughter but the sources do not call for a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Greens support separation of religion and state, implying no religious instruction in state schools, though this is not stated for schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bookchin rejects the state outright and wants it replaced, not strengthened.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bookchin's confederal model rests on assemblies and mandated, recallable deputies, so authority rests on citizens' continuing consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Greens favour local economies and reforming trade rules, rather than mercantile export aims.

population-transfer.rationale: The Global Greens call for a prohibition on collective expulsion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonviolence is a Global Greens principle, but the statement's absolutism covers property and Greens accept regulation; adherents differ.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Bookchin rejects the market's competitive grow-or-die logic and builds on cooperation and mutual aid.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources do not address party bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Bookchin opposes domination and the state as an alien power over people, but the republican formulation is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bookchin wants citizens to govern themselves in assemblies and criticises parliamentary parties, rejecting vanguards.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social justice is a core Global Greens principle, with aid priorities set with local communities.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Municipalists prize community-held housing and resist privatisation of public housing, but the sources do not discuss right to buy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Global Greens support workers' right to unionise.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Global Greens trace poverty to the economic system, corporate power and trade rules rather than to population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Bookchin prefers assemblies with recallable deputies; lottery is not discussed though sortition fits participatory democracy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Global Greens support human-rights protections, accountability for torture and the abolition of the death penalty.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The sources do not address price controls; Greens keep essentials publicly owned.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Global Greens support participatory democracy and independent civil society.

party-commands-army.rationale: Greens commit to nonviolence and separation of powers.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Global Greens defend migrants' rights, so long waits are disfavoured, though the sources do not address naturalisation.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Bookchin's model has mandated, recallable delegates who coordinate without ruling, consistent with citizen-level pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Bookchin criticises parliamentary parties but binds delegates to assembly mandates, not to party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Greens favour global partnership and strengthened multilateral bodies, though municipalists want power pushed down to localities.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Greens support separation of powers and civilian oversight and favour decentralised democracy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; the Greens only support separation of state and religion.

clerical-rule.rationale: Greens support separation of religion and state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The sources do not address this Marxist doctrine.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Respect for diversity and freedom are core Green values.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Bookchin wants recallable deputies and rotation of power; term rules are not stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Bookchin states that confederal deputies are recallable and mandated by their municipal assemblies.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Greens want to reduce arms and strengthen the UN, but the sources do not call for ending alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Green and municipalist programs defend tenants and community housing, not a ban on renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nonviolence is a core principle, though Bookchin favoured popular militias in a confederal setting; adherents differ.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Greens favour rural development but also limiting sprawl and dense cities; no claim of moral superiority.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources do not address national reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Green parties draw support from educated constituencies and nothing in the sources supports the claim.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Respect for diversity is a core Global Greens principle.

death-penalty.rationale: The Global Greens call for a worldwide end to the death penalty.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Global Greens support women's education and rights and gender mainstreaming.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Ecological wisdom and the Greens' science-based environmentalism, plus separation of religion and state, oppose teaching creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources do not address pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Greens defend asylum seekers' rights and respect for diversity, not descent-based citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Global Greens support the right of linguistic minorities to use their own language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The sources do not address exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Respect for diversity and freedom point toward encouraging nonconformity, though not stated about social pressure.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Global Greens call for reforming the World Bank and IMF and debt-for-nature swaps with community agreement.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Greens criticise neoliberal capitalism's global order, but the sources do not discuss independence directly.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Assembly democracy and participation fit an elected constituent assembly, though the sources do not discuss constitution-writing.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Greens reject growth as the aim and commit to rights and democratic participation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Global Greens support restructuring the world economy and aid set with local communities.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The Global Greens call for arms reduction and elimination of the arms trade and oppose nuclear arms expansion.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not address heads of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Greens criticise financialised neo-liberal capitalism and favour democratic oversight of finance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Greens favour peaceful conflict management through the UN, but the statement's context is not addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Bookchin places land and enterprise in community custody and Green programs subordinate property to ecological and social needs.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The sources do not address Soviet history, though Bookchin criticised nationalised economies.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Ecological wisdom and sustainability are core Global Greens principles and green politics applies precaution to environmental risks.

collective-defense.rationale: Greens want to reduce armaments and strengthen the UN, so military pacts are not a priority.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Greens support self-determination and the rights of peoples to a say in decisions affecting them.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Greens favour separation of religion and state but not state curbs on religious institutions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not address heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Greens commit to nonviolence and force only as a last resort against mass abuse.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Strengthening local autonomy fits the position, though the sources do not discuss it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rule by a sacred figure contradicts assembly democracy and recallable deputies.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Greens favour taxes serving social justice and redistribution, which flat taxes weaken.

character-from-environment.rationale: Bookchin's social ecology holds that society shapes people and citizenship is learned in assemblies, but the sources do not discuss innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of powers and accountability.

space-expansion.rationale: The Global Greens call for demilitarising space and for ecological limits.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Bookchin's democracy places power in the many through assemblies, not in a mix with the few.

equal-parenting.rationale: The sources do not address custody rules.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The sources do not address socialist states.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bookchin wants land under community custody, but the sources do not discuss redistribution from estates.

refugee-return.rationale: The Global Greens support asylum seekers and compensation for displaced peoples, which suggests a right of return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greens favour respect for diversity and nonviolence and oppose ethnic territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Greens support separation of religion and state and human-rights protections.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and political participation.

common-currency.rationale: The sources do not address currency unions; Green parties differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Greens favour local and global levels over ethnic unions, but not addressed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Global Greens support linguistic minority rights, though not specifically this model.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources do not address emigration versus equal rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bookchin rejected economic determinism in favour of social ecology, but the sources do not frame this directly.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Global Greens want corporate influence curbed and subsidies transparent, though the sources do not mention cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: The sources do not address bailouts; Greens criticise financialised capitalism but also bail-in ideas vary.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of powers and human-rights protections that constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Global Greens support women's political participation and gender mainstreaming.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Greens favour local economies but not imperial blocs, and oppose WTO-style liberalisation without closing trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The Global Greens want environmental, labour and health agreements to take precedence over trade rules.

moral-incentives.rationale: The sources do not address incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Nonviolence is a Global Greens principle, and municipalism builds assemblies openly.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Assembly democracy and equality are incompatible with hereditary rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Respect for diversity favours plural histories, though the sources do not discuss curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Global Greens support self-determination and compensation for colonial-era dispossession.

patriotic-education.rationale: Greens favour global partnership and peace and not nation-centred loyalty teaching.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Global Greens commit to defending the rights of people of colour and redress.

public-money-creation.rationale: Greens criticise financialised capitalism but the sources do not mention money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bookchin argues the grow-or-die imperative collides with ecological limits, but not about crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Greens support peaceful multilateralism and self-determination.

delink-world-market.rationale: Greens favour local economies yet also reform of global institutions; adherents differ.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources do not address this Marxist claim.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Global Greens commit to defending minorities, LGBTIQ+ rights and equality, which excludes a right to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Global Greens want rights such as a healthy environment written into the human-rights framework, but entrenchment against majorities is not discussed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The sources do not address colonial treaties, though Greens back Indigenous self-determination.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bookchin's order has no hereditary rulers; deputies are mandated and recallable by assemblies.

minority-veto.rationale: Bookchin lets a confederal majority block local actions violating rights or ecology and rejects consensus vetoes in his later writing; Green parties vary.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Bookchin's dual power challenges illegitimate state authority, but the sources do not address constitutional resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Municipalists locate sovereignty in assemblies rather than parliaments or monarchs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Global Greens call for humane treatment of animals in breeding, transport and slaughter.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The Global Greens demand humane treatment and ban growth hormones, accepting regulated animal use rather than abolition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Municipalists reject hierarchical charity and want equal citizens deciding together, though duty to others is valued.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Bookchin's whole project turns passive constituents into active citizens in assemblies.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Bookchin criticised consumer culture's effect on citizenship, but the sources do not state a media-pacification thesis.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The sources do not address hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Global Greens want the international economy restructured and criticise financialised neoliberal capitalism and IMF/World Bank rules.

native-born-offices.rationale: Greens defend migrants' rights and diversity, which oppose reserving office by birth.

party-own-road.rationale: The sources do not address communist parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Greens favour community-based economies but also support aid; the sources do not settle this.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Greens commit to nonviolence and peaceful conflict management.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Greens support Indigenous self-determination but the sources do not call for leadership over settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Respect for diversity and nonviolence make anti-fascism fitting, though constitutions are not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources do not address this comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Greens defend people of colour and equality and nothing supports minimising slavery.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the Greens' anti-racism commitments; the sources do not address monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources do not address men's disadvantage; Greens focus on women's rights.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources do not address domestic violence symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Respect for diversity cuts one way and universal human rights the other; the sources do not settle this.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Global Greens favour nonviolence, arms reduction and civilian control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Green politics measures well-being beyond GDP and supports women's economic security, though paying care work is not stated.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources do not address filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Bookchin wants citizens, not credentialed officials, to run public affairs.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Greens criticise corporate power but the sources do not address takeover review.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and autonomy, though divorce law is not addressed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Bookchin states that confederal deputies are mandated by municipal assemblies and recallable.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Greens criticise financialised capitalism and favour public provision of essentials.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Bookchin proposes land held in community custody rather than private ownership, though not exactly use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The sources do not address budget approval.

single-official-language.rationale: The Global Greens support the right of linguistic minorities to use their own language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The sources do not address foreign land ownership, though community control of land appeals.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The Global Greens defend people of colour, but legal tests for discrimination are not discussed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Global Greens describe consumption in industrialised countries as excessive and call for well-being rather than GDP and a zero-waste economy.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Global Greens want arms trade eliminated and force only under UN mandate.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Global Greens state that corporations have gained outsized influence over governments.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Greens favour open civil society and global partnership, though corporate funding of politics is opposed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Greens do not propose population growth and accept migration, though the sources do not discuss these incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local control of land and housing fits municipalism, but the sources do not discuss residency limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: The sources do not address job guarantees; Green parties vary.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Global Greens support democratic multilateral institutions and peaceful conflict management, though the thesis is not discussed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Bookchin challenges the state's legitimacy but values democratic decisions of assemblies.

non-intervention.rationale: The Global Greens allow UN-mandated force against genocide, so absolute non-intervention is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources do not address union structure; Bookchin rejects union-run economy.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Respect for diversity and defence of minorities make such conspiracy claims unacceptable.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Greens support marriage equality, which presumes a legal institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Participatory democracy requires open information, and Greens demand transparent subsidies and open process.

local-production.rationale: The Global Greens back community-based economies and reversing rural drain, and green municipalism puts economic change at municipal scale.

informal-organisation.rationale: Bookchin opposes informal anarchist organisation and builds formal assemblies and confederations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Global Greens support the ICC and human-rights bodies, so international law matters.

religious-nation.rationale: Greens support separation of state and religion and respect for diversity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Global Greens favour democratic multilateral institutions on equal footing.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Municipal self-governance suggests local revenue control, but the sources do not state it and Greens also support solidarity.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Bookchin treats land and enterprises, not personal belongings, as community held.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Global Greens favour peaceful conflict management and no Cold War positions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Greens keep essentials public but welcome community provision; sources are silent on mixes.

religion-illusion.rationale: Respect for diversity and spiritual ecology in green thought oppose treating religion as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Bookchin saw capitalism as ecologically destructive though historically productive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Global Greens tie women's rights to ending the sale of sex and organs as economic security strategies and to broader economic redesign.

socialized-care.rationale: The sources do not address care provision.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Respect for linguistic diversity opposes purging language.

treaties-binding.rationale: The Global Greens support the UN Declaration on Indigenous peoples as a minimum standard, though treaty permanence is not addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Municipalism builds self-governing communities with shared resources and community land trusts, though not all property is common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Respect for diversity and Indigenous land rights oppose settling majorities in minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Bookchin rejects both capitalism and nationalised collectivism, favouring a third route of municipal confederation.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources do not address this; Greens favour self-determination and peaceful settlement.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Greens defend minorities and condemn atrocity crimes, so denial is rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Global Greens call for decriminalising same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Participatory democracy and freedom are core Global Greens principles.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Greens support separation of state and religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Global Greens back self-determination and restructuring the world economy in favour of poorer countries.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The sources do not address Islamic doctrine; nonviolence is a Green principle.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Nonviolence and participatory democracy exclude removing rulers by religious war.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participatory democracy is one of the six core principles of the Global Greens Charter, and Bookchin's assemblies are its municipal form.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Global Greens link gender, race, disability, sexuality and economic justice in one program.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Global Greens call for legal recognition of transgender people.

assisted-dying.rationale: The sources do not address assisted dying; Green parties vary.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Green politics often claims to be beyond left and right, while Bookchin placed himself on the left; adherents differ.

alienated-labor.rationale: Bookchin criticises capitalism's effect on people but the sources do not use alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Respect for diversity and minority rights reject this claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority from participatory democracy is the Greens' basis, not divine source.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Greens favour separation of state and religion but also minority rights; green parties are split on bans.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The Global Greens oppose sexualised violence and support accountability.

social-market-economy.rationale: Greens criticise neoliberalism but also want more than a regulated market, so adherents differ.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Global Greens aim at reducing arms and demilitarisation but allow UN-mandated force in extremis.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Greens favour arms reduction and UN strengthening over blocs.

rich-first.rationale: The Global Greens favour social justice and restructuring the world economy and reject uneven growth.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Greens favour community-based economies but the sources do not mention mutual credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Global Greens call for reforming the IMF and World Bank and criticise neoliberal capitalism.

property-franchise.rationale: Equality and participatory democracy exclude property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Bookchin's social ecology holds that domination of nature stems from domination of humans, and Greens link gender and ecology.

reification.rationale: The sources do not use this concept.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Global Greens say corporations hold outsized influence, though press ownership is not discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Greens support separation of powers and accountability, though the doctrine is not discussed.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Global Greens defend the rights of people of colour and commit to equality and participatory democracy.

online-participation.rationale: Bookchin insists on face-to-face assemblies, while other green municipalists use digital tools; adherents differ.

open-government-data.rationale: The Global Greens demand transparent subsidies and participatory process, and municipalists publish proposals.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Respect for diversity and equality oppose such restrictions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Respect for diversity and defence of minorities oppose targeted boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Participatory democracy supports deliberative citizen bodies, though Bookchin prefers open assemblies to chosen samples.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The sources do not address religious doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Global Greens say wealthy corporations have outsized influence over governments.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Global Greens support LGBTIQ+ equality across government, though military service is not addressed and Greens are wary of militaries.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Greens support separation of state and religion and respect for diversity.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Greens oppose the death penalty and favour rights, but the sources do not call for abolishing police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The sources do not address consociationalism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Greens want public provision and social justice, not reliance on charity.

term-limits.rationale: Bookchin favours recall and rotation but term limits are not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources do not address existential risk; Greens prioritise ecological risk generally.

vote-delegation.rationale: Bookchin binds deputies by assembly mandates and recall, not by individual liquid delegation.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and political participation, though religious offices are not addressed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and equality.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Municipalism grounds citizenship in participation in the community, so residents vote locally; Global Greens defend migrants' rights.

rent-control.rationale: Municipalist movements target housing affordability and gentrification, though the sources here do not state rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources do not address patents and copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Nonviolence and participatory democracy oppose drilled national youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The Global Greens oppose nuclear arms and call for arms reduction.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Global Greens favour demilitarisation and arms reduction, though bases are not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The Global Greens call for accountability for mass atrocity and genocide.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Bookchin invokes from each according to ability and places enterprise in community custody, against rentier income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nonviolence is a core Green value but absolute pacifism is not stated and the Greens accept last-resort force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Greens base politics on local communities and respect diversity, not ancient national continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources do not address this.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nonviolence opposes honouring martyrdom for the nation.

racial-pride.rationale: The Global Greens defend people of colour against discrimination but promote respect for diversity over racial group politics.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Bookchin treats politics as civic citizenship, not spiritual warfare.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The sources do not address diaspora homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: The sources do not address this.

god-not-male.rationale: The sources do not address theology.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The sources do not address religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Respect for diversity and minority rights oppose ethnic economic control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The sources do not address this.

independent-unions.rationale: The Global Greens support workers' right to unionise and independent civil society.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Bookchin rejects workers' control as the basis, but sources do not address socialism's definition.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Global Greens state that essentials such as water should be publicly owned and controlled, and Bookchin puts local enterprise in community custody.

second-chamber.rationale: Bookchin proposes a confederal council of delegates, which is not a second chamber; sources do not address it.

municipal-property.rationale: Bookchin proposes land and enterprises held in community custody, rejecting both private owners and nationalised state enterprise.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Bookchin states that municipalities link through recallable deputies mandated by assemblies for coordination and administration, leaving policy with local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: The sources do not address the family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Ecological wisdom and the precautionary outlook of Greens favour caution on regulation, though drugs are not discussed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources do not address ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The sources do not address payment privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Greens' civil-liberty outlook favours privacy but the sources do not address it.

person-over-state.rationale: Bookchin places citizenship and community above the personal and vocational interest while rejecting the state, so the claim fits only partly.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources do not address spirituality, though some Green strands do.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Municipalism places power with local assemblies, so revocable local powers contradict it.

gm-crops.rationale: The Global Greens restrict hormones and antibiotics in animals and favour precaution, but GM crops are not mentioned.

dense-cities.rationale: The Global Greens call for limits on urban sprawl, which favours density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Greens focus on equal rights and respect for diversity, not on racial group organisation.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Global Greens allow force only as a last resort under a UN mandate.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Greens favour diversity and local communities rather than language-defined nations.

communal-electorates.rationale: Greens favour participatory democracy and secular state, not separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports such conspiracy claims.

free-public-college.rationale: The Global Greens reject treating education as a tradable commodity and support social justice.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The Global Greens call for eco-taxes and ecological limits so that polluters pay.

future-generations.rationale: Sustainability is a core principle of the Global Greens Charter, which commits to protecting the Earth for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Some ecofeminist Greens hold this but the sources do not state it and adherents differ.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Global Greens call for regulating the arms trade with the aim of eliminating it and for demilitarising space.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Global Greens favour democratic and transparent multilateral institutions, though secret treaties are not addressed.

capital-controls.rationale: The Global Greens support a financial transactions tax to curb speculation, though not capital controls specifically.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Bookchin proposed confederal militias and Greens are cautious of arms; the sources do not settle it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nonviolence suggests support for refusal of unjust wars, though the sources do not state it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Global Greens support workers' right to unionise.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The sources do not address tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Greens criticise neoliberal austerity, so binding fiscal rules are disfavoured.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Global Greens call for restructuring international economic rules in favour of poor countries, reforming the WTO, IMF and World Bank.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Bookchin wants to displace the state through dual power rather than taking it over, yet green municipalists govern city councils; adherents differ.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Bookchin sets the economy to be settled in practice by assemblies, but also sets a community-custody principle.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecological wisdom values nature in itself; pricing nature as capital is a minority Green view.

sacred-nation.rationale: Greens favour global partnership and local community, not sacred nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The Global Greens favour education access and debt reform, though student debt is not addressed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The sources do not address this concept.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The sources do not address human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: The Global Greens reject treating media and culture as commodities.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The sources do not address this.

farm-price-support.rationale: The sources do not address farm support, though Greens back rural development.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Global Greens oppose nuclear arms and call for arms reduction.

workers-own-party.rationale: Bookchin rejects class-based parties for municipal citizen politics, while Greens form their own parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and treat sexualised violence as a crime, with FGM protection part of their women's rights program.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and equality.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources do not address this.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Greens favour regulation, eco-taxes and an international court over corporate ecocide, not tort-only liability.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The sources do not address chiefs, though Indigenous self-determination is supported.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Greens give ecological wisdom a primary place yet commit to freedom and rights; adherents differ on conflict cases.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Greens favour rights and rehabilitation, so fixed mandatory sentences are disfavoured, though not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Greens support minority language rights but integration policy is not discussed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The Global Greens support the right to unionise, though compulsion is not discussed.

voter-id.rationale: Participatory democracy favours broad access, though voter ID is not discussed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Separation of state and religion and respect for diversity imply no privileged interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Participatory democracy demands active citizen decision-making beyond competitive elections.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Participatory democracy and freedom oppose cutting off communication.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Global Greens support women's autonomy and rights, though morality of premarital sex is not addressed.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Global Greens support women's political participation and equal rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The sources do not make this claim and Greens respect diversity.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Global Greens oppose racism, but the sources do not discuss race's scientific basis.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Global Greens support gender mainstreaming across government.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Bookchin places land in community custody rather than first-use ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The Global Greens support the ICC and an international court for corporate environmental destruction.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Greens support separation of state and religion and science-based ecology.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Global Greens support Indigenous self-determination and women's political participation together.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Bookchin rejects nationalised planned economies, so he would not call for defending a bureaucratic state.

indirect-election.rationale: Bookchin's confederation uses delegates chosen by assemblies, which resembles this, but he stresses direct decision in local assemblies and recall.

national-church-status.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of state and religion.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Global Greens support self-determination and linguistic minority rights, and municipalism favours local autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Greens favour participation of affected people in decisions, though plebiscites are not discussed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The sources do not address borders.

simple-living.rationale: The Global Greens describe consumption as excessive and call for sufficiency, though not full self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Greens support Indigenous land rights but not specific settlement restrictions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Greens oppose conscription, so equal-conscription is disfavoured.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The sources do not address this.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Global Greens call for a worldwide end to the death penalty and accountability for torture.

close-ties-china.rationale: The sources do not address this.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Greens favour multilateral peaceful relations and not ethnic kin-state protection.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Bookchin places land in community custody, in line with common ownership of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: The sources do not address self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Greens favour eco-taxes and consumption reduction, so cutting consumption taxes is disfavoured.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Greens favour universal public provision of essentials.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Bookchin's order rests on citizen assemblies and delegates, and rejects leader-centred bypassing.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Global Greens want corporate subsidies transparent and harmful ones phased out.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Global Greens support separation of state and religion.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Greens favour sustainable futures rather than ancestral restoration.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Global Greens support women's rights and equality.

national-resource-control.rationale: Greens favour community control of resources over national or foreign control, so the sovereignty frame fits only in part.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Respect for diversity is a core Global Greens principle, and Bookchin builds common citizenship across ethnic and gender lines.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Global Greens allow force only under a UN mandate and favour self-determination, so bloc intervention is rejected.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources do not address feminist theory; Greens support women's rights and gender recognition without stating this view.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Greens favour public provision of essentials over replacing welfare with a cash payment, but the sources do not discuss it.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the Charter's commitment to equality and social justice, which judges distribution by fairness of outcomes and Bookchin's view of property as a source of exploitation.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The Global Greens Charter states the Greens will work to implement a Tobin-Henderson or Financial Transactions Tax to curb speculative international currency transactions.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The Charter names systematic exclusion of racial, ethnic, national and religious communities as a democratic failing and commits to equality and respect for diversity.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not stated; inferred from nonviolent direct action and the municipalist claim that popular assemblies hold legitimacy above state law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not stated; inferred from Bookchin's view that technology can free people from toil for civic life and the Green stress on social over economic ends.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the confederal model of many self-governing municipalities and Green opposition to the IMF and World Bank order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not addressed by green municipalists; Bookchin was Marxist-influenced but moved away from class analysis, so inferred as neutral.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred; the tradition is internationalist and municipalist, treating the nation-state as the problem and civic identity as local and confederal.

material-over-identity.rationale: The Charter lists equality, respect for diversity and participatory democracy beside economic justice, and does not subordinate identity issues to workers' material interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Green municipalism rejects party-state rule and nationalization in favour of assemblies, confederal deputies and municipal community control.

missingStatements.text: Environmental policy should be made and carried out by towns and cities rather than by national governments.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim of green municipalism: environmental change should arise from action in the municipality, not from state or national policy.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should meet in local face-to-face assemblies to decide public policy, with higher levels only coordinating.
missingStatements.rationale: Bookchin's model makes policy local and leaves administration to confederal deputies mandated by the assemblies.

notes: Wikipedia's article is brief and gives no list of principles, so positions rest on Bookchin (the assembly strand) and the Global Greens program (the green-party strand). Bookchin rejects syndicalist workers' control and national nationalization, while pragmatic city parties govern within the state; answers on those points are lower confidence.
